body:
MEASURED ADDITION TO Q5: the current resolver is proposal-order sensitive under the exact equal-evidence boundary case.

I tested exact current commit 6ec8b698277ebde0377ca61892aa8c6b5c1500a5 in a clean archive. The scratch court builds one Ordinary Boundary bundle with equal calibrated proposals for 412 and 413, resolves it, reverses only proposals, and resolves again. ResolveSuite result: 22 passed, 1 failed. Forward obtained Accepted(412, 0.95); reversed obtained Accepted(413, 0.95).

The source explains the result. collect records first-appearance order from substantive.map(_.value.get).distinct.zipWithIndex; resolve chooses minBy(weighted, order). When provider count, proposal count, score presence, and raw score tie, input order selects the accepted value.

The existing property named "resolution is deterministic" compares resolve(f,b,p) with itself. It proves repeatability for one ordering, not permutation invariance. No current court forbids asynchronous provider arrival order from changing the licensed cut.

This is not a claim that every discrete claim resolver must erase declared priority. It is decisive against reusing this resolver unchanged for recall boundaries: arrival order is neither boundary evidence nor a construction policy. The proposed PROPOSAL-PERMUTATION INVARIANCE court should therefore be an R0 red court, not merely a future design preference. It must compare both the resolved state and any identity/receipt derived from the complete proposal bundle.

Scratch only: /private/tmp/storymodel4s-boundary-permutation.Oh58ht. No repository source edited; no vocabulary, ADR, bead, path, or implementation authority claimed.
